how: Every tile was looked at on the contact sheet. Eleven sources were then opened at 1400 px from tools/seed/.imgcache: nos. 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 18. Three of them were cropped and enlarged: the GRT 455's hull decal and console, the DB/37's stern (to look for outboards), and the 1095 Fly's roof (to tell the Fly from the Coupé). data/northside/images.json and heroes.json were checked by address and by file name, and they hold none of these 18. The price file's formosa-grt-tiller-1 frame, which is already held, is a different picture from nos. 1 and 5. Fifteen pictures were opened in all. The nine accepted Jeanneau frames are the right boats, but jeanneau.com's Legal Notice says the photography belongs to SPBI S.A. Each one therefore carries a licence line and must not be held or printed until the importer or SPBI gives permission.

verdicts.reason: The whole boat on the water, with one driver at the tiller. It comes from the GRT Tiller range page. The frame is pixel-identical to Formosa's own GCBC-GRT-425-Tiller-take-off.jpg, so the builder's own file name identifies it as the GRT 425 Tiller. It is not the price file's held formosa-grt-tiller-1 frame, which is a different picture. No render of this model exists, so a scene is the catalogue copy. It is held at 1100 from a 1919 source, so nothing is enlarged.
verdicts.depicts: Formosa GRT 425 (Tiller), whole boat taking off on open water with one person aboard (boat_formosa: Formosa - GRT 425 (Tiller))
differs: the tiller outboard's make and power are not readable, so the caption must not name the motor a quote line carries

verdicts.rule: an interior, console or detail shot proposed as a whole boat; a render of a different colourway than the row
verdicts.reason: Looked at at 1400 px. It is a tight crop of the cockpit, with two people filling the middle of the frame. The bow is cut off at the right edge and the outboard at the left. It is the 495 (495 and SRT are on the hull), but it is not a whole-boat picture. It also comes from Formosa's choose-your-colour page, and its own name (FM_495-Side-Con_Formosa-White-Interrior-CLOSE) says it shows one interior colour option on a pale hull. That makes it a colourway picture, not the model's catalogue card. A gap is honest. A 495 side view or a render named for the model would close it.

verdicts.rule: people or text over the boat that makes it unusable; not shown to be that exact model
verdicts.reason: Looked at at 1400 px. The boat sits on a trailer in another dealer's showroom. TOWNSVILLE MARINE is printed on the hull beside 565 and painted on the back wall. Four other Formosas and their motors fill the rest of the frame. The bow is out of frame on the left, so the picture cannot show the open cushioned bow and walk-through screen. Those are what would tell the X Bowrider apart from the 565 Side Console, Territory, Centre Console and Centre Cabin. A competitor's name on the boat cannot go beside a Northside Marine quote line. When in doubt, reject: the 565 X Bowrider stays a gap.

Looked at at 1400 px. One whole Haines Signature cuddy runabout sits on a dual-axle trailer at a launching ramp, with the Signature script on the hull. The picture is in the gallery of the builder's own 545F page, and its file name (545_W2) agrees with the page. That meets the Haines rule: file name plus model page. Unlike the 620BRX set, page and file name agree. It is a ramp scene, not a studio shot or a hero, so it is a catalogue copy only. The frame is portrait: 1067 x 1707 at the source and held at 688 x 1100, so nothing is enlarged. A card should fit the whole frame rather than crop it to landscape, or the boat ends up under 700 px wide.
verdicts.depicts: Haines Signature 545F, whole boat on a Dunbier trailer at a ramp, bimini stowed (boat_haines: Signature Fisher - 545F)
differs: The boat is on a branded Dunbier trailer, and the tailgate of the tow vehicle is at the left edge. A quote may carry a different trailer or none, so the caption must not imply the trailer is included
the outboard's make and power are not readable

It is a different frame from no. 1: planing, not take-off. No people or text cover the boat. It is held at its source size (1917 x 845) and is not enlarged to 2560.

verdicts.reason: Looked at at 1400 px. A black-hulled Formosa hardtop runs past a beachfront, and no length is readable on the hull. The only identification is the 2019 file name F715HC, which says Half Cabin, not Enclosed. Formosa built a separate Lockable Half Cabin in that period: its own 755 spec sheet is headed "755 LOCKABLE HALF CABIN", a model distinct from the Enclosed Half Cabin Hardtop. The current site sells no 715 to compare against. Filing this frame to SRT 715 Enc (Half Cabin) is an inference, not something the picture shows. When in doubt, reject. It stays a gap until Formosa or Northside names the boat.

verdicts.rule: not that exact model (a sister variant)
verdicts.reason: Looked at at 1400 px, with the stern cropped. The DB/37 badge on the hardtop is readable, but the transom shows a bare swim platform and no outboard cowlings. From this raised angle, twin outboards would stand clear above the platform. The DB/37 is also built as an inboard. This header slide is on the OB page, but Jeanneau reuses frames across a model's variants, and this picture does not show the DB 37 OB that the row prices. When in doubt, reject. A frame that shows the outboards would settle it.

It is the cover image of Jeanneau's own DB/43 OB page, and the DB/43 IB page carries a different cover. It is held at its source size of 1920 x 1280, not enlarged.
